evidence_quotes.quote: This program has succeeded in increasing household access to proper toilets.
Interviews with local officials indicated that limited coordination between various stakeholders,
informants noted that the maintenance of sanitation facilities is often neglected after the initial phase of the program

rationale: Qualitative policy evaluation (in-depth interviews with 10 village/cadre/resident informants, documentation, and field observation) of the Open Defecation Free (ODF) program in Tambak Osowilangun Village, Surabaya. Two governance mechanisms are co-equally central across the effectiveness, efficiency, and supporting/inhibiting factor analyses: participation_assistance (active community participation from planning to monitoring, Great Surabaya Cadre volunteers, community sanitation committees, and NGO counseling/cooperation) and institutional_structure_coordination (municipal policy and dedicated budget allocation, procurement administration, and inter-organizational coordination across the city government, health office, sub-district officials, and NGOs). Outcomes span both primary_connection (household access to proper toilets increasing from ~40% to ~90%) and effective_access (functional sustainability, ongoing toilet maintenance, water availability for sanitation, and sustained utilization vs reversion to open defecation), alongside intermediate administrative procurement delays.
